protocol_type: Bit-oriented synchronous data link protocol; frame-based with I/S/U frame discriminator, sliding-window sequence numbering, and link-management U-frame command/response set.

opcodes.name: RR
opcodes.description: Receive Ready — positive acknowledgement; cancels prior RNR; can also be used by primary with P-bit to solicit secondary status.

opcodes.name: REJ
opcodes.description: Reject — go-back-N negative acknowledgement; requests retransmission starting at N(R).

opcodes.name: RNR
opcodes.description: Receive Not Ready — acknowledges packets but throttles peer until further notice.

opcodes.name: SREJ
opcodes.description: Selective Reject — requests retransmission of only N(R); optional functional extension.

opcodes.name: SNRM
opcodes.description: Set Normal Response Mode (3-bit sequence numbers, 1-byte control field).

opcodes.name: SNRME
opcodes.description: Set Normal Response Mode Extended (7-bit sequence numbers, 2-byte control field).

opcodes.name: SARM
opcodes.description: Set Asynchronous Response Mode (3-bit sequence numbers).

opcodes.name: SARME
opcodes.description: Set Asynchronous Response Mode Extended (7-bit sequence numbers).

opcodes.name: SABM
opcodes.description: Set Asynchronous Balanced Mode (3-bit sequence numbers, peer-to-peer).

opcodes.name: SABME
opcodes.description: Set Asynchronous Balanced Mode Extended (7-bit sequence numbers).

opcodes.name: SM
opcodes.description: Set Mode generic — new in ISO/IEC 13239; carries an information field selecting parameters including 15-/31-bit sequence numbers.

opcodes.name: SIM
opcodes.description: Set Initialization Mode — vendor-specific secondary initialization (e.g. firmware download).

opcodes.name: RIM
opcodes.description: Request Initialization Mode — secondary requests primary to send SIM in lieu of DM.

opcodes.name: DISC
opcodes.description: Disconnect — terminate logical link; secondary acknowledges with UA and enters disconnected mode.

opcodes.name: RD
opcodes.description: Request Disconnect — secondary requests primary to send DISC.

opcodes.name: UA
opcodes.description: Unnumbered Acknowledge — secondary's acceptance of an acceptable mode-set or DISC command.

opcodes.name: DM
opcodes.description: Disconnected Mode — secondary is in disconnected state; rejects any command other than acceptable mode-set.

opcodes.name: UI
opcodes.description: Unnumbered Information — unacknowledged datagram-style data; no sequence number; loss is undetected.

opcodes.name: UIH
opcodes.description: UI with Header Check — ISO/IEC 13239 addition; FCS covers only a configurable-length header prefix.

opcodes.name: UP
opcodes.description: Unnumbered Poll — group polling; solicits a response from a secondary; used in SDLC.

opcodes.name: RSET
opcodes.description: Reset — reset secondary's receive sequence number to 0 (ABM only).

opcodes.name: XID
opcodes.description: Exchange Identification — exchange link-level capabilities; ISO 8885 information-field format.

opcodes.name: TEST
opcodes.description: Test — ping/loopback; TEST response echoes the TEST command payload.

opcodes.name: FRMR
opcodes.description: Frame Reject — unrecoverable error response carrying W/X/Y/Z/V error flags.

channels.name: Synchronous serial link
channels.description: Single bit-synchronous serial channel; NRZI-encoded on the wire; bit stuffing applied between flags.

channels.name: Asynchronous serial link
channels.description: Single asynchronous octet channel (e.g. RS-232 with start/stop bits per byte); control-octet transparency via 0x7D byte stuffing.

channels.name: Multidrop bus (SDLC)
channels.description: Single shared link with one primary terminal and multiple secondary terminals addressed by Address field; primary polls each secondary in turn.

frame_types.name: I-frame (Information)
frame_types.purpose: Carries user data; includes N(S) send sequence + P/F + N(R) receive sequence (3-bit or 7-bit).

frame_types.name: S-frame (Supervisory)
frame_types.purpose: Flow + error control without information field: RR / RNR / REJ / SREJ.

frame_types.name: U-frame (Unnumbered)
frame_types.purpose: Link management — mode set, disconnect, frame reject, XID, TEST, UI.

frame_field_layout.value: 1 byte (default) or extended (multi-byte; top bit = 0 means continue)
1 byte normal / 2 bytes extended; encodes I/S/U + N(S) + N(R) + P/F + U-frame M-bits
Opaque payload (0..N bytes); present in I-frames and some U-frames (UI/UIH/XID/TEST/SM/FRMR); ABSENT in S-frames
CRC-CCITT (poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF) — 16 bits default; or CRC-32 (poly 0x04C11DB7) — 32 bits optional

control_field_encoding.lsb_first_note: All control-field bits are transmitted least-significant-bit first; the I-frame discriminator is therefore the FIRST transmitted bit (a 0).

s_frame_types.name: RR
s_frame_types.purpose: Receive Ready — positive ack; cancel prior RNR; primary may use with P-bit to solicit secondary status.

s_frame_types.name: REJ
s_frame_types.purpose: Reject — go-back-N negative ack; sender retransmits starting at N(R).

s_frame_types.name: RNR
s_frame_types.purpose: Receive Not Ready — acknowledges but throttles peer.

s_frame_types.name: SREJ
s_frame_types.purpose: Selective Reject — retransmit only N(R); optional.

u_frame_subset_minimum_required: Commands: I, RR, RNR, DISC, and one of {SNRM, SARM, SABM}.
Responses: I, RR, RNR, UA, DM, FRMR.
valid_ready_handshake_rules: There is no AMBA-style per-cycle VALID/READY handshake — HDLC is frame-level.
Per-frame acknowledgement is piggybacked on N(R) in any I or S frame.
Flow control via RR (resume) / RNR (pause) / REJ (go-back-N retransmit) / SREJ (selective retransmit).
Mode-set commands are acknowledged with UA (acceptance) or DM/FRMR (rejection).
P/F bit serves as a checkpoint token — only one in flight on the link at a time.
byte_order_within_information_field: LSB-first within each octet on the wire; multi-octet field byte-order is implementation-defined.

interframe_state.abort: Seven or more consecutive 1-bits without a 0-bit (synchronous); 0x7D 0x7E (asynchronous incomplete byte-stuff).
interframe_state.frame_sharing: End-flag of one frame MAY be shared as start-flag of next (single shared 0x7E).
